title: Add Repo Checks
bottom_line: Run /plan-tools:hook-finalize-pr to write .claude/finalize-pr.md: your repo's own checks, such as lint or migrations, that finalize-pr runs before it opens the pull request.

sections.heading: Run it, optionally describing the steps you want

blocks.code: /plan-tools:hook-finalize-pr [optional description of the steps to add]
blocks.caption: With a description, Claude uses it. Without one, Claude looks through the repo and suggests steps.

before.label: With a description
before.text: Claude writes the steps you described.

after.label: Without one
after.text: Claude inspects the repo and proposes at most 5 candidate steps, then asks which to keep.

blocks.text: It works interactively: it inspects the repo, proposes steps and writes `.claude/finalize-pr.md`, a file of free-form markdown instructions. Use it to create the file or to edit an existing one.

blocks.title: Where Claude looks for candidate steps
items: `Makefile`
`package.json` scripts
`pyproject.toml`
CI workflows
`migrations/`
`CHANGELOG*`
version files

blocks.title: When to use it
items: You want to configure, add, change or review repo-specific finalize-pr checks, such as lint, migrations, version bumps or a changelog.
You say "set up the finalize-pr hook".

terms.definition: The /plan-tools:finalize-pr skill. The steps in your file run as its step 3b.

nodes.label: Test plan, user flows

nodes.label: Your repo steps

blocks.title: How the file is used
items: It lives at `.claude/finalize-pr.md` at the top of the repo. If it is empty or missing, the step is skipped.
A Sonnet helper reads it word for word, with no other context, so it is written as plain instructions.
On a first run the pull request does not exist yet, so steps must not use `gh pr ...`.
On an incremental run the helper is told the `$BASE..HEAD` range that changed since the last finalize, and each step says whether to look only at that range or run in full.
The helper commits its own fixes and reports what it fixed and what it found but did not fix. The unfixed findings become residual work.

sections.heading: Each step says what to run, when, and what if it fails

cards.title: The exact command
cards.text: Checked to exist in the repo.

cards.title: When it applies
cards.text: For example, "if `migrations/` changed in the diff".

cards.title: On failure
cards.text: Fix and commit, or report only.

blocks.caption: Every step is a numbered instruction written as a command.

blocks.title: What steps may not do
items: Ask questions while running. Steps are non-interactive.
Give a different result when run twice. Steps are idempotent.
Push, open or edit the pull request.
Need secrets.

blocks.title: An example file
blocks.code:
1. Run `make lint` and fix what it reports. Scope to files in `git diff --name-only $BASE..HEAD` when a range is given.
2. If `migrations/` changed, check every new migration has a downgrade; fix and commit if missing.
3. If `src/` changed, bump the patch version in `pyproject.toml` once per branch (skip if already bumped vs. the base branch).
blocks.caption: From the skill.

blocks.title: A shorter example
blocks.code:
1. Run `make lint` and fix what it reports.
2. If `migrations/` changed, check the new migration has a downgrade.
blocks.caption: From the README.

sections.heading: Your existing file is never overwritten without asking

cards.title: File already has content
cards.text: Claude shows you what is there.

points.text: It asks whether to add, change or replace. It never overwrites without your confirmation.

cards.title: No commit by default
cards.text: Claude writes the file and does not commit it unless you ask.

sections.heading: You end up with the file written and shown to you

before.label: Before
before.text: finalize-pr skips step 3b because `.claude/finalize-pr.md` is empty or missing.

after.label: After
after.text: `.claude/finalize-pr.md` holds your numbered steps, and Claude shows you the final content. It creates the `.claude/` folder if needed.

reference.title: About the plan-tools plugin
items: Plugin purpose: plan-driven workflow tools that bootstrap a new web or mobile app end to end, split implementation plans into context-sized resumable sessions, and drive them to PRs.
Installing plan-tools also installs the plugins it depends on: `ntfy`, `fastapi-template` and `htmx-vs-alpine`.

No environment variables are needed. The one setting, `designer_ui_review` (default `false`), is changed with `/plugin configure plan-tools@wovemind`. It runs the ui-change-guard designer review (/ui-change-guard:review-ui-change) before finalize-pr raises a PR.
